archive_17_001.speaker: narrator
archive_17_001.text: The village street shone orange beneath the smoke when Yue reached the safe meeting point. The packing-room windows glowed, then vanished behind a dirty roll of air. The response crew had blocked the street nearest the workshop and was bringing people to the assembly room's clean side. Tan carried the emergency rack's four clean blankets. Dai kept the path behind her clear. Yue heard He Xi calling his father's name from his family's doorway, and saw his mother catch his coat before he ran towards the blocked entrance.

archive_17_002.speaker: narrator
archive_17_002.text: The foreman met Tan beyond the smoke line. Two workers were already outside; the father had been found in the front bench room and was coming through its checked exit with a trained crew member. The owner stood beside a bucket line, his face streaked by soot. He began telling Dai what had burned before she asked who was still inside. He stopped, looked towards the crew and named one remaining worker being guided out. Dai stayed beside him until the foreman confirmed that person's arrival at the clean side.

archive_17_003.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_17_003.text: Tell the foreman where people work, which doors they use and what may still be live. I shall hold your papers when he says they can safely come out. I do not need an inventory while somebody is missing. Look at him, not at the packing window. He is asking you about the back passage.

archive_17_004.speaker: narrator
archive_17_004.text: He Xi's father emerged bent forward, one hand held against his chest and the injured one hanging stiffly by his coat. He was walking with help, not carrying anybody. The crew member took him directly to the clean assembly-room entrance, where the village clinician had established the first assessment place. He Xi started after him and obeyed the clinician's instruction to wait outside the working space. His mother gave the doctor the relevant hand history when asked. She had used her whole strength stopping their son and was trembling now that there was nowhere sensible to put it.

archive_17_005.speaker: he_xi
archive_17_005.text: Father, I am here. Mother is here. The doctor wants us out of her elbow space, so I shall stand where you can see my coat. You do not need to tell me anything about the workshop tonight. If you need something, ask her first. I can be a very good courier when somebody gives me one actual message.

archive_17_006.speaker: narrator
archive_17_006.text: His father nodded, tried to speak and coughed instead. The clinician checked his breathing and the present condition of the injured hand, then continued her independent assessment. He Xi's mother wanted to ask whether he would be well by morning. She asked what the clinician needed from her now. The answer was the medicine he already used and a warm dry layer from their own room. She sent their son for those specific items along the cleared street. He went quickly enough to feel useful and slowly enough not to fall.

archive_17_007.speaker: narrator
archive_17_007.text: Tan found the heater's diagram on the outside service board with the owner. The packing fire had begun when a shifted guard let loose wrapping fall against the hot housing. The feed stone's six-unit charge was spent; four units had become working heat and two remained trapped in the frame. The ordinary release handle was too hot and obstructed to operate safely. The crew could smother the burning packing, but wanted the retained charge grounded before approaching the metal frame. The owner authorised Tan to use its prepared remote release circuit.

archive_17_008.speaker: narrator
archive_17_008.text: The circuit had a ground receiver rated for four units and a separate quarter-unit command gate. Tan and the workshop's trained keeper checked the receiver, cleared its surrounding space and tested the lead continuity with the unpowered meter. The diagram matched the installed fittings. Yue's inspected archive cuff could provide a short command through that gate from the clean exterior position. The stored frame charge would go to the prepared receiver, not through her body. Tan pointed to the full-release mark and asked Yue to repeat the stopping sequence before they connected her stitch.

archive_17_009.speaker: tan_ke
archive_17_009.text: Quarter-unit useful command, through this fitted gate. Your gross delivery will be the measured half-unit we have checked with this cuff. The two trapped units belong to the frame's discharge path. Hold the command only for the marked interval, release fully, then let the keeper test the frame. If the gate fails, we stop. We do not ask your channels to become the missing handle.

archive_17_010.speaker: narrator
archive_17_010.text: Yue stood on the dry protected board beyond the smoke line. Her measured available reserve was twenty-four above her stopping floor. The quarter-unit sampling check left twenty-three and three-quarters. She aligned the four pairs through the external cuff-to-sole stitch, felt the prepared command path settle and gave the half-unit gross pulse. A quarter reached the gate as useful command. The release marker moved. Beyond the cleared receiver, two trapped units drained through the fixture's rated path with a brief pale glow. She fully discharged before lifting her heel.

archive_17_011.speaker: narrator
archive_17_011.text: The keeper's ordinary frame test found the retained charge gone. Yue's quarter-unit post-check left twenty-three in her available reserve. Her calf remained quiet during the ordinary movement away from the board. Nothing in her body had borne the frame's two-unit store. Tan disconnected the inspected cuff and passed the clear test to the foreman. The burning wrapping did not vanish with the glow. The crew continued its ordinary smothering work, with the metal approach now safe under the verified state. Yue watched people do the part which her command could not.

archive_17_012.speaker: narrator
archive_17_012.text: A worker brought a dry cover over the last small flame while another removed the unburned packing beyond the hot zone. The foreman kept the bucket line from splashing onto the live-check area until the keeper cleared it. Water then cooled the separate smouldering wood under the crew's direction. Smoke thickened for a moment and drifted along the blocked street. The public reading room's loan carrier was nowhere near this fire; Yue was absurdly relieved by that irrelevant thought, then turned back when Tan asked for the next clean blanket.

archive_17_013.speaker: narrator
archive_17_013.text: Three archive blankets went to people in the clean assessment space, leaving one unissued in Tan's kit. The clinician's ordinary village response supplies covered immediate treatment and its own warm room. He Xi returned with his father's medicine and coat, carrying them separately from the blanket he had nearly grabbed at the door. His father could speak a few words now. He complained that the coat had his better buttons. His mother said he could spend tomorrow admiring them if the clinician agreed, and the clinician answered that tomorrow would need another actual assessment.

archive_17_014.speaker: lin_yue
archive_17_014.text: I have your father's coat, He Xi. Give the medicine to the doctor and let her finish the question she asked. Your mother wants the coat, not a heroic explanation of why you ran faster than the street allowed. The buttons appear to have survived. I think he may complain about them for some time yet.

archive_17_015.speaker: narrator
archive_17_015.text: He Xi laughed once, a broken sound which became a frightened cough. His mother took the coat and laid it where the clinician instructed. Yue stayed outside the working space with the empty medicine wrapper. The father had known where the uncharged service door stood and had directed the younger worker towards it before the crew reached them. That useful action did not make his sore lungs or injured hand imaginary. He looked frightened when his wife asked why he had stayed for the evening inventory, then she put her hand on his shoulder and let the question wait.

archive_17_016.speaker: narrator
archive_17_016.text: The last worker was accounted for. Nobody had disappeared into an unrecorded back room. The foreman kept the damaged packing area closed while his crew checked the roof edge and hot remnants. The owner asked whether his bench drawings could be retrieved from the front room. The foreman sent a trained pair through the already cleared approach, not the smoking section, and they brought the dry front tray to him. Tan accepted its safe temporary support at his request. The burnt rear shelves held other work, and no one promised those sheets had survived because some had.

archive_17_017.speaker: narrator
archive_17_017.text: One of the two younger workers had slept above the packing room; the other's rented bed was in its now-closed rear annex. Their immediate lodging had burned or become unsafe. The owner was arranging paid replacement rooms in the village, but the clean beds would not be ready that night. Dai checked the archive's two available temporary guest places, previously used during the storm and now empty. The clinician would assess both men before any move. He Xi's father had his own family room and would return there only under the clinician's actual plan, with his wife beside him.

archive_17_018.speaker: narrator
archive_17_018.text: The foreman handed the owner a stopped-work notice for the damaged room, then led the last cooling check while the street's orange light faded. Yue looked down at her gloves and saw soot which had reached them without her ever approaching the flames. Her half-unit command had been precise. The smell in the street was anything but precise: burnt cloth, wet timber and the ordinary winter supper somebody had abandoned when the bell rang. Tan folded the unused blanket over the disconnected cuff. Behind the clean-room door, He Xi was asking his father which button he meant.

archive_17_019.speaker: narrator
archive_17_019.text: The assembly room smelled of clean water beneath the smoke carried in on coats. He Xi's father sat where the clinician placed him, with his feet on the dry floor and his better coat across his knees. He wanted to explain the guard before the owner thought him responsible. The clinician told him to rest his voice. His wife said the owner could wait. He glanced at her, saw that she meant it and put the explanation down like a tool somebody else could hold for a while.

archive_17_020.speaker: narrator
archive_17_020.text: The owner had remained outside with the foreman. The heater keeper described the shifted guard, the loose packing and the retained charge in their actual order. Its last routine check had not recorded a fault in the remote release; that circuit had worked. The physical release handle had become inaccessible in the fire, and the ground receiver had passed its actual check before use. Tan added her brief command record. The foreman wanted the facts needed for the stopped-work inspection. He did not ask anyone to make the account sound like a successful exhibition of advanced cultivation.

archive_17_021.speaker: narrator
archive_17_021.text: One of the young workers had been packing completed pieces when the guard moved. He feared the loss would be deducted from his wages. The owner said no such decision had been made and that the ordinary earned wage record would be reconstructed from surviving records before any claim was discussed. The worker asked whether he could take his bedding from the closed loft. The foreman refused access until the damaged floor had been assessed. The worker stopped arguing about money and looked towards the black upper window, where most of his small possessions had been.

archive_17_022.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_17_022.text: We have two temporary guest places upstairs at the archive. Dai has checked them. The doctor must decide whether the short walk is suitable, and the place is only for people she clears to move. If your loft stays closed, the owner will arrange the longer lodging. Tonight you need not prove that the bed you lost was inexpensive enough to replace. Tell us what the doctor says you need, and we shall start there.

archive_17_023.speaker: narrator
archive_17_023.text: Luo had arrived with the archive's rostered receiving attendant after confirming cover at the gate. He carried no private source papers and proposed no extract which could make a house safe. The two men listened to him because he was offering actual clean places which Dai had checked. The clinician assessed their smoke exposure and the one worker's minor wrist burn, dressed it and set the follow-up instructions. Both were stable for the short guided walk under the present conditions. Neither required the archive to substitute for clinical observation if symptoms worsened.

archive_17_024.speaker: narrator
archive_17_024.text: The village response kitchen had already given the men their evening food during assessment. They took that meal at the clean room, so the archive issued none when they arrived later. The clinician gave the named receiving attendant the care instructions needed for the stay, with the men's consent, and kept the unrelated history at her own desk. A follow-up was arranged for the next morning. The guide checked the path report before starting. Tan carried the folded spare blanket while the two men walked at the clinician's advised pace, supported where needed by the trained attendant.

archive_17_025.speaker: narrator
archive_17_025.text: He Xi's father could return to his own family room after the clinician's present assessment, with his wife and son beside him and the specific warning signs they had been given. The next examination would take place in the morning. He Xi held the medicine, his mother carried the coat and the father used the sound hand for ordinary balance. They did not ask the injured hand to close around a heavy arm. Yue watched the family reach their checked doorway, then followed Tan uphill with the guest group. The street's fire glow had gone out behind them.

archive_17_026.speaker: narrator
archive_17_026.text: At the archive, the guest room had two prepared temporary beds and a clear path to the attended corridor. Their clothing stayed away from the source shelves; wet outer things went to the ordinary residential drying place. The attendant checked the clinician's immediate instructions and the contact plan before the men settled. Dai authorised an extra half-sack of charcoal for the late warming and half a cooking bundle for boiled water. Those issues came after the day-one-hundred-and-fourteen close and would enter the next report. Warmth was no longer a general promise somebody could make without opening a store.

archive_17_027.speaker: narrator
archive_17_027.text: One man stared at the clean blanket as though accepting it might establish the size of his debt. He asked when the archive wanted payment. Dai told him it was temporary emergency shelter under the accepted board arrangement, with his longer lodging being arranged by his employer. She did not ask him to donate a memory of the fire in exchange. The other man wanted to know whether anybody could bring his boots from the loft. Tan said access remained closed. They could ask the owner about actual replacement boots in the morning.

archive_17_028.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_17_028.text: There is a bell pull beside the bed. The attendant is the person receiving it tonight, and she knows the doctor's instructions. Use it if the symptoms on the sheet appear, or if you need help getting up. You are not disturbing a manuscript by needing a person. The corridor is a residential corridor. It was checked for two guests before we brought you here.

archive_17_029.speaker: narrator
archive_17_029.text: The men settled with the two issued blankets. The third used blanket, returned from the father's care space, was isolated for washing; the fourth remained clean and unissued in the kit. The winter shelter did not become a storeroom for the whole workshop. Dai accepted the dry front tray only in the separate safe staging room at the owner's written request, with its visible condition listed. Its safe retrieval had not made every rear shelf recoverable. Tan put the disconnected cuff on its normal inspection rack and wrote the used command beside its return.

archive_17_030.speaker: narrator
archive_17_030.text: Luo offered Yue a cup of boiled water from the added warming issue. She wrapped both hands around it and felt the smallest tremor in her fingers. The command had stopped correctly, and the calf was quiet. Her body was still answering the bell, the orange windows and He Xi's mother's hand gripping his coat. Luo said nothing about calm mastery. He took the chair beside her and complained that the herb would surely require a fresh support after being left near the draught. She laughed, and the cup stopped rattling against its saucer.

archive_17_031.speaker: narrator
archive_17_031.text: Tan came in with the sealed command note for the fire inspection. She had checked it for the gross half-unit, useful quarter-unit and the frame's separate two-unit discharge, with no new stage claimed. She asked Yue to read what actually concerned her before signing. Yue did, corrected the time of her full release and signed. The page went to the foreman's incident file through the owner-authorised contact. Tan then pulled off her coat and said the notebook margin she had spent days drying now seemed almost politely damaged. Yue told her paper could be inconsiderate without needing a competition.

archive_17_032.speaker: narrator
archive_17_032.text: The late round passed the guest room twice. Both men slept between checks, and the attendant kept the actual care notes brief. He Xi's family door remained closed, with his mother taking the agreed first watch before her son relieved her. She had told her village kitchen supervisor about the morning clinical appointment and arranged her paid shift change through the normal cover. Her husband did not need her to become an invisible unpaid worker in three places. He needed the coat, the medicine and the person who had made him stop explaining before he could breathe comfortably.

archive_17_033.speaker: narrator
archive_17_033.text: Yue went to bed with soot beneath one glove seam and no appetite for washing it theatrically. She put the glove with the proper dirty kit and used the ordinary basin. In the next room a guest coughed once, then the attendant's quiet footsteps answered. The archive's four blankets had become two on beds, one awaiting washing and one still in the rack. Down in the village, the workshop floor remained closed under the foreman's notice. The night's work had stopped the fire and made room for people. Morning would reveal what else had been lost.

archive_17_034.speaker: narrator
archive_17_034.text: The morning inspection on day one hundred and fifteen divided the workshop into a safe front room and two closed areas. The packing loft's floor needed qualified repair before anybody entered it. The heating frame remained disconnected and would require its own assessment. In the front room, the owner's cash box was intact. He counted sixty-eight copper with his business clerk, then checked the last wage receipt against the surviving daily slips. Six bench drawings had burned in the rear drawer. Thirteen in the rescued front tray survived with smoke on their outer covers.

archive_17_035.speaker: narrator
archive_17_035.text: Tan returned the tray after its listed temporary staging, at the owner's request and along the foreman's cleared approach. She had not accessioned it into the archive or opened every sheet because the fire had made its owner tired. He now asked for help comparing the surviving wage slips with the current workers' own records. Dai approved one ordinary advisory interval. Each worker could choose which relevant receipt to show. The rear workbook had lost several pages; the front slips still held names, dates and totals. Help could begin with those actual surviving fields.

archive_17_036.speaker: narrator
archive_17_036.text: The young worker with the dressed wrist brought a pocket slip he had kept folded inside his bed cover. It survived because it had been in his coat during the fire. Its two shift marks agreed with the business clerk's surviving daily record. Another worker's memory placed a half-day repair on the wrong date. His own paid receipt showed the earlier date, and he corrected his account without being accused of lying. Tan kept the correction beside the stated source. The workshop needed the amount owed, not a competition for the person who remembered winter most impressively.

archive_17_037.speaker: narrator
archive_17_037.text: Luo worked with the business clerk under the new paid advisory interval, matching only the fields the owner and workers had authorised. The archive's stamp did not turn the reconstructed wage sheet into a complete untouched workbook. It remained a new account based on identified slips, receipts and stated recollections. Twenty-four copper in earned wages was verified and paid from the intact purse, leaving forty-four. The clerk gave each worker an actual receipt. The two sheltered men could buy small necessities without waiting for the workshop's future insurance assessment to become money.

archive_17_038.speaker: narrator
archive_17_038.text: The owner reserved sixteen of the remaining copper for four nights' replacement lodging and meals for the two men from day one hundred and eighteen, at the accepted local rate. The rooms were in a sound village house inspected for its present use. Twenty-eight copper remained for his other immediate commitments. The workshop's mutual-loss association would assess the damaged room under its existing membership, and its reply was pending. He did not call that pending claim a cash balance. He also did not ask the archive to hide his private lodging bill in the winter pantry.

archive_17_039.speaker: narrator
archive_17_039.text: He Xi's father received his verified wages through his own receipt, then returned to the clinician rather than the bench. His lungs needed more rest, and his hand had stiffened after the night's fright. The workshop honoured the paid recovery days in his actual appointment, drawing on its own remaining work reserve. The clinician would reassess him before any return to bench tasks. His wife kept her adjusted village kitchen shift, while their son completed one short paid route. They had a household to feed, and nobody's fear had stopped the ordinary price of beans.

archive_17_040.speaker: narrator
archive_17_040.text: He Xi came uphill later with no private file, only the collection receipt he was hired to deliver. When the public queue ended, he asked Yue to walk as far as the yard. He said he had wanted his father's appointment to make him stay, and now he hated the appointment for giving him a place to be hurt. The words came out too fast. Yue waited by the new threshold while he stared at the snow beside the path. He looked younger when he was not arranging somebody else's safe delivery.

archive_17_041.speaker: he_xi
archive_17_041.text: If I had told him we could manage without his wages, perhaps he would not have taken the evening inventory. But I liked being able to say he had a real job here. I liked the paper with the notice period. It sounded as though leaving had to become something he explained before doing it. I did not ask whether that meant I was asking the workshop to keep my father for me.

archive_17_042.speaker: narrator
archive_17_042.text: Yue asked what his father had said about staying before the fire. He Xi answered that he had wanted the bench work because it was work his hand could do. Then he rubbed his own fingers together, angry at the answer's ordinary shape. He had wanted a sentence which made him responsible enough to change what happened. Yue said he could ask his father again when the clinician allowed a longer conversation. He could not answer for him merely because guilt sounded more powerful than waiting beside a coat.

archive_17_043.speaker: lin_yue
archive_17_043.text: Ask him what he wants now. Let him answer while he is alive and in the room. Your fear knows a great deal about you, and very little about the choice he would make if you stopped making it inside your own head.

archive_17_044.speaker: narrator
archive_17_044.text: He Xi laughed bitterly at himself and then apologised for making the yard sound like a family hearing. Yue said he had asked her to walk, not to judge. They went back to the door, where Luo was holding the public road folder he actually needed to deliver. The folder gave him a useful end to the conversation. He accepted its ordinary paid task and left along the checked path. His father had not become an archive record whose heading could keep him from moving. He Xi seemed relieved by that and offended that it was true.

archive_17_045.speaker: narrator
archive_17_045.text: Tan spent the next inspection interval beside the owner in the safe front room. The surviving bench drawings named a maker where the commissioning slip had one, including the father's rail adjustment. Smoke had darkened several cover edges without changing the legible dimensions. Six rear originals were gone. A retained customer copy preserved one lost cabinet pattern, but not the maker's original working corrections. The owner wanted to remake all six from memory before spring orders resumed. Tan asked which dimensions the surviving evidence actually supported. He stared at the empty drawer and began with one.

archive_17_046.speaker: narrator
archive_17_046.text: The damaged room's new plan moved combustible wrapping away from the heater housing and gave the checked guard its own clear working space. The keeper would inspect the repaired frame before its next charge; the fire's successful remote release did not certify the rest of the apparatus sound. Ordinary tools could work in the safe front room while the other areas remained closed. The owner offered the younger workers those light assigned tasks after clinical clearance, not a heroic clean-up inside the burnt loft. They were pleased to earn something with their hands besides a story about their escape.

archive_17_047.speaker: narrator
archive_17_047.text: Sun heard about the lost drawings from the owner when he asked for the public trade directory. She did not offer to remember dimensions she had never seen. She asked whether he had a pattern which he wanted to make differently now. He said he had never liked the cabinet lid. She told him the lost lid might at least permit an honest new design if he stopped calling it an exact restoration. He looked annoyed and then interested. She bought no tragedy from the conversation; she took home an umbrella notebook and left him considering a hinge.

archive_17_048.speaker: narrator
archive_17_048.text: On day one hundred and seventeen, the supplier sent the carriage dispatch receipt. The approach had passed the loaded-route assessment, and the balanced wagons carried four hundred and eighty-three food shares, forty charcoal sacks and fifty cooking bundles. The archive arrival remained day one hundred and nineteen under the current weather. The damaged first shares were replaced in that food total without extra charge. Tan set the receipt beside the first delivery record and left the new goods outside current stock. The room had enough to wait through the reported journey without pretending the wagons could not be delayed.

archive_17_049.speaker: narrator
archive_17_049.text: The first guest wanted to leave as soon as the owner's new rooms were named. He disliked sleeping uphill from the work he had lost, and the dressed wrist made him anxious about missing his place at the safe front bench. The clinician's day-one-hundred-and-seventeen check found him improving but kept the practical limits on his task. The second man had slept poorly and asked whether the room's bell pull could be taken to the new lodging. Dai said he should ask its owner how help was reached there. She sent that actual question ahead before the move.

archive_17_050.speaker: narrator
archive_17_050.text: The receiving house provided a named night contact, clean beds and an ordinary warm room separated from its stored trade goods. The owner paid the agreed lodging amount from his own reserved sixteen copper. The clinician approved the short transfer for first light on day one hundred and eighteen, after a present check of both men. They would eat breakfast at that house under its meal arrangement. The archive's attendant gave its contact the care instructions the men had authorised. No private workshop account travelled in the care cover simply because both papers concerned the same fire.

archive_17_051.speaker: narrator
archive_17_051.text: At first light the check took place, the path was open and the two men walked with the trained attendant to the receiving house before archive breakfast. They wore the replacement boots their employer had actually provided. The borrowed blankets returned to the archive's dirty-linen place, joining the one already isolated after the father's care. Two temporary beds became empty again. Dai signed the actual departure time and the receiving contact's acknowledgement. The men had used three full archive food days, the hundred-and-fifteenth through the hundred-and-seventeenth, without remaining guests in tomorrow's kitchen plan.

archive_17_052.speaker: narrator
archive_17_052.text: Luo had left a small public road extract on the first man's bedside table at his request. The man remembered it before departing, folded it into his own pocket and asked whether taking it was allowed. Its ordinary issue receipt was already his. Luo answered yes, then watched him descend without offering another explanation. The man wanted to find his cousin's village when the longer roads opened. His future was not the archive's to arrange simply because it had given him a bed. He carried the map with the careful attention he had given his first clean blanket.

archive_17_053.speaker: narrator
archive_17_053.text: The owner came later for the staging receipt and found the guest places closed correctly rather than retained for the workshop's convenience. He thanked Dai, then asked what help the public desk could offer with the lost cabinet pattern. She named an appointment within its ordinary service and the evidence he should bring. He had a retained customer copy and a current redesign, which were different things. He did not have to pretend either was the burned original to begin again. The owner put the appointment time in his own business book beside the planned room inspection.

archive_17_054.speaker: narrator
archive_17_054.text: Tan's fuel keeper completed the last drying checks that afternoon for the agreed one-copper return fee. Winter qualified work fell from one hundred and three to one hundred and two. Two more sacks passed and re-entered usable stock. The last sack failed: its contents had broken down and remained unsuitable for the approved stove issue. Tan recorded its disposal under the keeper's ordinary safe method. Of the six excluded sacks, five had actually recovered; one was permanently lost. The two consumed drying sacks had still been consumed. No part of the work made that loss embarrassing to write down.

archive_17_055.speaker: narrator
archive_17_055.text: The laundry attendant washed the three used emergency blankets in the ordinary safe washing place, with an extra half cooking bundle for the larger hot-water batch. The cloth dried fully before returning to the clean rack. Four emergency blankets were available again, including the one never issued. Tan checked them and found one small worn corner which she marked for ordinary mending. He Xi offered his mother's contact out of habit, then caught himself. She had her village shift and her own commissions. The archive could use its proper housekeeping arrangement instead of borrowing her future hours through her son.

archive_17_056.speaker: he_xi
archive_17_056.text: I keep hearing a useful task and immediately thinking who in my family can do it. Mother has started asking whether I have already sold the afternoon before speaking to her. I think she is right. I shall mend that sentence before I offer anybody's needle again. Your blanket can wait for the person you actually employ to look at it.

archive_17_057.speaker: narrator
archive_17_057.text: The four resident days used forty food shares. Six guest shares for the three full shelter days left three hundred and twenty-six and a half. Four normal heat sacks and the late fire-night half-sack, offset by the two newly recovered sacks, left twenty-five and a half usable charcoal sacks. No damp sacks remained waiting for acceptance. Four normal cooking bundles, the late half-bundle for warm water and the extra half for blanket washing left forty-five and a half. Tan closed the report before the supplier's approaching wagons could improve any of those actual numbers.

archive_17_058.speaker: narrator
archive_17_058.text: He Xi's father came to the public desk only after the clinician permitted an ordinary short outing. He brought the large copy of his appointment and asked the reading assistant to show him its recovery-day provision again. He understood it but wanted to remember the wording without his son's anxious voice in his head. The assistant read the relevant lines and let him ask his own questions. He would return to limited bench work after a new assessment, not because the fire had ended or the workshop needed him. He folded the page and took it home himself.

archive_17_059.speaker: narrator
archive_17_059.text: His wife met him at their doorway with a pot from her own kitchen. She asked whether he had decided to stay through the workshop repair. He said he wanted to, if the proper light tasks resumed. She asked whether that was work or a way to avoid explaining another departure. He answered that it might be both, then asked her what she wanted before he promised anything. She looked so startled that he smiled. He Xi heard the conversation from the inner room and did not come out to provide the correct answer.

archive_17_060.speaker: narrator
archive_17_060.text: Sun had begun the umbrella story's second page. Its owner tried to sell the hole as a special view of the sky. The umbrella objected that it had been promised a patch, not a reputation. She showed the teacher the line during a visit, pleased with its foolishness. The teacher laughed and asked whether the umbrella might keep the hole after discovering that it liked stars. Sun said it might, but that would have to be the umbrella's decision. She crossed out one word and left the page messy. The story was still alive enough to refuse a neat answer.

archive_17_061.speaker: narrator
archive_17_061.text: Tan received a short relay acknowledgement from her old school. The publication board had received the request and would compare the retained classroom sheet with the revised lesson book. Its acknowledgement was not the correction she wanted. It did mean somebody had been assigned the comparison. She put the actual receipt with her own letter and went back to the safe rack work. The burned cabinet drawings made the distinction between a retained design and a remembered design newly sharp, but she refused to make the workshop's loss evidence of who had drawn her old pattern.

archive_17_062.speaker: narrator
archive_17_062.text: At evening close, the owner sent the foreman's continued restriction for the damaged packing room and the actual safe-front-work list. The mutual-loss assessment remained pending. The workshop had wages paid, two workers in arranged lodging and a new ordinary job list which respected present clinical limits. It also had an unsafe floor and six original drawings it could not retrieve from ash. Dai accepted the update needed for the archive's own temporary support record and returned the unrelated business papers unopened. The fire had ended. Its work had not.

archive_17_063.speaker: narrator
archive_17_063.text: Yue checked the cuff's return condition with Tan before the next practice interval was scheduled. The used command had stayed inside its inspected envelope, and the current lead showed no damage from the night. Her calf remained quiet under ordinary movement. She put her own command note beside the training sheet rather than using the successful release as an argument to raise the next load. When Tan asked what she wanted to practise, she said making the stop equally clean when nobody's workshop was burning. Tan wrote that down as a reasonable ambition and offered her the next safe interval.

archive_17_064.speaker: narrator
archive_17_064.text: The watcher brought the evening carriage report while the supper pot was warming. The wagons had reached their arranged intermediate stop under the inspected loads; tomorrow's arrival remained conditional on the morning route check. Yue's hundred-and-nineteenth day would be her weekly rest, and Tan had already assigned the receiving checks without her. She could watch from her room if she wished. She could also close the curtain. The thought pleased her more than another heroic task would have done. Outside, the empty temporary guest windows reflected the yard lamp, while the village workshop's burnt windows stayed dark.
